reason: This passage (Exodus 1:6-12) describes a new Egyptian pharaoh who, driven by fear of the growing Israelite population, implements oppressive policies including forced labor and enslavement. While the pharaoh does take action, he does so purely out of self-interest and paranoia, not from genuine responsibility for his people's welfare. Critically, the narrative demonstrates the failure of this approach—the more the Israelites are afflicted, the more they multiply and grow. The text presents this as a cautionary example of leadership motivated by fear and self-preservation, not as a model of good leadership based on accountability and care for people's welfare. The oppressive results ultimately harm both the oppressed and undermine the stated goals.
